summary.a: Generic indie Japan travel/itinerary PDFs on Etsy and Gumroad cluster at $9.73–$24.21 (median ~$21.60 among listed prices), with a coaching/video bundle outlier at $67. Enhanced regional guides on Lemon Squeezy run $17–$30. GPSmyCity's single-route audio walks are $0–$5, with $12.99–$18.99/year for all-city access. None of these include archival citations, then-and-now aerial imagery, translated disaster memorials or a bibliography — the Area Dossier's real differentiators versus this entire category.
summary.b: Pricing here is bimodal. Cheap automated UK property-record pull-ups cost $12.63–$25.34 (HouseDossier) with no human narrative. Human-staffed record lookups run $18–$34/hour-equivalent (Dorset Council, Past Discoveries). Fully bespoke, individually researched and written narrative house-history reports cost far more: $635–$995 in the US (WashingtonHistory.com) and AUD $1,700–$6,000 (~$1,122–$3,960) in Australia (The House Detective), i.e. roughly 25–50x the automated tier, because each report is commissioned once for one property.
summary.c: Koseki/family-register lookups and translations run $30–$50/hour or ~$25/page at nonprofit/community services aimed at descendants (Densho, CertTranslate). Commercial Japan-genealogy specialists aimed at the same diaspora audience charge $100/hour (Japan Genealogy Connect) and $108–$118/hour effective inside large multi-hour agency packages (Legacy Tree: $2,950/25hrs, $10,800/100hrs). The broader US professional-genealogist market spans $50–$200+/hour. Median effective rate across all c comparables is about $100/hour.

dossier.why: Generic Etsy/Gumroad Japan itinerary PDFs sell for $9.73–$24.21 (median ~$21.60) despite being templated content with no original research. The Area Dossier's cited 1,500–2,500-word history, then-and-now 1940s aerial photography, translated disaster memorials, ground-formation maps and bibliography put it in a different content class — closer in depth to what UK/AU house-history researchers charge $150–$1,700+ for bespoke single-property work, except it is productized once per district and resold to many buyers rather than commissioned per customer. $14.99 prices it clearly above the generic-template pack and near the upper end of enhanced indie guides (Lemon Squeezy's $17–$30 regional guides) while staying an impulse buy for history-minded travelers and Nikkei descendants. $9.99 as a launch price matches the single most common indie anchor price seen across Gumroad and other shops, useful for building early reviews. If a cheaper 'automatic' tier is kept alongside the full Dossier, it should sit near $6.99–$8.99 (in line with GPSmyCity's per-route price and HouseDossier's automated Quick Check at $12.63).

deepResearch.why: Japan-specific specialists serving diaspora clients charge $100/hour (Japan Genealogy Connect) to $108–$118/hour effective inside agency packages (Legacy Tree). Even 1.5–2 hours of that professional-rate archive/register research plus assembling a written report already approaches $190–$235, so the owner's $190 idea is well-grounded market-wise (not underpriced relative to nonprofit koseki rates of $30–$50/hr, and a bargain next to Legacy Tree's $2,950 for a 25-hour package). Recommend holding at essentially the same level, rounded to $195.

Bespoke narrative property-history reports that involve dedicated researcher fieldwork run $635–$995 in the US and the AUD equivalent of roughly $1,100–$4,000 in Australia. The originally proposed +$200 jump (to $390) for adding an actual on-site visit, travel and logistics is thin next to that market. Raising the increment to about +$230 (total $425) still undercuts every bespoke on-site comparable found, while better covering the researcher's on-site time and travel.
